title: verified-set idle statistics (T04, offline, no engine, no training)
question: why does training on chosen_verified_cand (the verified-set argmax) produce a higher idle share and a worse closed loop than executed_cand?

s1_verified_set_size.question: how big is the verified set?
s1_verified_set_size.reading: every one of the 19,772 slots carries exactly one engine-verified candidate: |S| = 1 for 19,772/19,772, and |S| = 0 and |S| > 1 never occur.  This is the direct consequence of the frozen fast profile's verify_k = 1 (RESLOT_2F.md §6.2), so the histogram is a spike, not a distribution.

s2_idle_in_verified_set.question: does the verified set contain idle (candidate 0)?
s2_idle_in_verified_set.reading: idle is the single verified candidate on 8,774/19,772 = 44.38% of slots.  Because |S| = 1 everywhere, 'idle in S' and 'the verified argmax is idle' are the *same event*; the two counts below are identical by construction, not by coincidence.

s3_chosen_verified_is_idle.question: is the verified-set argmax idle, and does that depend on |S|?
s3_chosen_verified_is_idle.reading: 8,774/19,772 = 44.38% of slots have idle as the verified argmax, and 0/19,772 have no verified target.  The |S| stratification is degenerate: only |S| = 1 exists, so the argmax never chooses between two verified candidates.  The informative stratifications are by decision-frame offset (43.90% vs 44.85%, i.e. flat) and by the executed action (88.75% idle when the executed action was idle, 18.83% when it was not).

s4_executed_is_idle.question: is the executed action idle (the A0 target)?
s4_executed_is_idle.reading: 7,225/19,772 = 36.54% overall, but this rate is NOT frame-stationary: 43.83% at the legacy block's first decision (frame 4i) versus 29.25% at its second (frame 4i+2).  The verified column is flat across the same two groups (43.90% vs 44.85%).

s5_disagreement_buckets.question: on the slots where chosen_verified_cand != executed_cand, which direction does the disagreement go?
s5_disagreement_buckets.reading: 6,288/19,772 = 31.80% disagree, which reproduces T04's 6,288 exactly.  Of the 6,288: 2,362 (37.56%) are 'executed moved, verified is idle', 813 (12.93%) are the reverse, and 3,113 (49.51%) are two different non-idle actions; no slot has an empty verified set.  The net idle injection is 2,362 - 813 = 1,549 slots = 7.83 pp, which equals the gap between the two columns' idle rates (44.38% - 36.54% = 7.83 pp).  Splitting by decision-frame offset localises it completely: 6,227 of the 6,288 disagreements (99.03%) sit on the legacy block's *second* decision (frame 4i+2); on the first decision the two columns agree on 9,825/9,886 = 0.9938 of slots.

s6_idle_position_in_verified_set.question: where does idle's score sit inside the verified set?
s6_idle_position_in_verified_set.reading: degenerate, and that is the finding: on all 8,774 slots where idle is verified there is no second verified candidate to compare against, so idle is the sole verified candidate 8,774/8,774 = 100.00% and the categories 'unique max', 'tied max', 'below max' are each 0/8,774.  With verify_k = 1 the question 'is idle the max *within* S' has no content: every member of S is trivially its own max.

s7_ties.reading: 0/19,772 slots have a tie at the maximum of teacher_scores, and 0/19,772 have a tie inside the verified set; the conditioned questions ('does S cover all tied maxima?') are therefore not_available (empty denominator), not zero.  chosen_verified_cand is the unique global argmax on 19,772/19,772 = 100%.  Ties do exist, but only among the 17 *unverified* scores: 17,453/19,772 = 88.27% of slots have more than one unverified candidate at the top of the unverified sub-ranking, and they never change the choice because the verified candidate is separated from every unverified one by at least exactly 5.0 score units (the unverified_discount; margin min = p05 = median = 5.0 on all three shards).  So a tie-break, lowest-index rule is not load-bearing anywhere in this corpus.

s8_attribute_A0v_idle.question: is A0v's idle rebound just a faithful reflection of the target distribution?

marginal_divergence.note: both marginals are over the same 19,772 slots, so a non-zero divergence is a pure label-column difference, not a sample difference

published_holdout_crosscheck.source: evidence/T04/TRAIN_CONTROLLED.md §5.1 (same 15,819 train / 3,953 holdout rows this script counts)
published_holdout_crosscheck.note: CE minus the *marginal* entropy of the arm's own target is a lower bound on the irreducible term (the true one is H(Y|X) <= H(Y)), so this is NOT a generalisation gap.  It only shows that A0v's 0.160-nat holdout CE advantage is smaller than its 0.224-nat lower entropy floor, so the published holdout numbers do not support 'the chosen_verified target is the easier one to fit'.

s8_attribute_A0v_idle.reading: the target columns' idle rates are 44.29% (chosen_verified) and 36.23% (executed) on the 15,819 train rows, a contrast of 8.06 pp; the measured arm contrast is 20.66 pp (first-death) and 16.49 pp (standard S1N), so the labels account for 39%-49% of the measured gap.  A0v sits 5.2-6.3 pp ABOVE its own prior and A0 sits 3.2-6.3 pp BELOW its own; both deviations are outside the two 95% intervals.  So the target distribution is a necessary and quantitatively measured part of the explanation, but 'A0v is just fitting a ~50%-idle target' is not what the data says: the target is 44.3% (train) / 44.7% (holdout).

attribution.question: is A0v's idle rebound a faithful reflection of the target distribution, or an optimisation failure?

criterion.statement: if |measured idle - target idle prior| is small relative to the two 95% intervals overlapping, the policy's idle rate is what the target distribution predicts and the difference between arms is a target-side difference; a measured rate well outside the prior interval would instead point at an optimisation / distribution-shift effect
criterion.note: the eval protocols (first-death, S1N) are not the training distribution, so this is a marginal plausibility check, not a distributional identity

verdict.judgement: target distribution contributes and is necessary, but is NOT sufficient; the tie-break/argmax hypothesis is refuted; a 5-6 pp residual is unattributed by these statistics

hypotheses.statement: the verified argmax systematically picks idle because idle ties at the maximum and the lowest-index rule favours candidate 0
hypotheses.evidence: |S| = 1 on 19,772/19,772 slots, so no slot ever compares two verified candidates; 0/19,772 slots have a tie at the maximum of teacher_scores; 0/19,772 have a tie inside S; chosen_verified_cand is the unique global argmax on 100% of slots.  The lowest-index tie rule is never exercised.

hypotheses.statement: the chosen_verified column genuinely carries more idle than the executed column, so a faithful fit must idle more
hypotheses.evidence: 44.29% vs 36.23% on the 15,819 train rows (8.06 pp, 1,275 net slots); 44.73% vs 37.79% on holdout; the net idle injection over all slots is 2,362 - 813 = 1,549 slots = 7.83 pp.

hypotheses.statement: A0v's idle rate is just its target's idle rate
hypotheses.evidence: A0v is 0.5055 / 0.4952 against a 0.4429 prior (+0.0626 / +0.0523, both outside the 95% interval), and A0 is 0.2989 / 0.3303 against 0.3623 (-0.0634 / -0.0320, also outside).  The measured arm contrast is 2.0-2.6x the label contrast.  The published holdout CE advantage of A0v (0.160 nats) is smaller than its lower entropy floor advantage (0.224 nats), so the holdout numbers do not rescue 'the chosen target is simply cleaner/easier'.

hypotheses.statement: the idle gap between the columns is produced by the teacher's verify stage preferring idle
hypotheses.status: refuted, replaced by a sharper mechanism
hypotheses.evidence: the verified column's idle rate is flat across the legacy block's two decisions (43.90% / 44.85%), while the executed column's drops from 43.83% to 29.25%.  The gap is created on the executed side, at the second decision of the legacy four-frame block (frame 4i+2), where executed_cand is the second element of a plan committed two frames earlier while chosen_verified_cand is a fresh query at that frame.  6,227/6,288 disagreements (99.03%) live there, and on the first decision the two columns agree on 9,825/9,886 slots.

hypotheses.statement: the remaining 5-6 pp is an optimisation or behaviour effect
hypotheses.evidence: these fields cannot separate closed-loop dynamics from optimiser path effects.  The dev protocols idle more than any training prior even for the frozen baseline (B0: 45.81% / 46.10% against a 36.23% executed prior), so a label prior is not a point prediction for a closed-loop rate.

testable_criterion.statement: a label prior is a point prediction only if the closed-loop rate of a policy that fits that label matches the label's own idle rate; here the prior intervals [0.4352, 0.4506] and [0.3548, 0.3698] exclude the measured 0.4952-0.5055 and 0.2989-0.3303, so the criterion fails for BOTH arms in opposite directions
testable_criterion.reading: this asymmetry (A0v above its prior, A0 below its) is why the answer is 'target-side plus an unattributed behavioural term', not 'target-side only'

decisive_next_experiment.rationale: on the legacy block's first decision the two target columns are statistically the same label (idle 43.90% vs 43.83%, identical action on 99.42% of slots), and on the second decision they are wildly different (44.85% vs 29.25%).  This gives a matched ablation that needs no engine and no new data.
arms: A0-slot0: executed_cand CE on the 9,886 first-decision rows only
A0v-slot0: chosen_verified_cand CE on the same 9,886 rows
A0-slot1 / A0v-slot1: the same pair on the 9,886 second-decision rows
decisive_next_experiment.prediction: if the target distribution is the cause, A0-slot0 and A0v-slot0 must land on top of each other (their labels are the same distribution) and the whole arm gap must reappear between A0-slot1 and A0v-slot1; if the gap survives on slot 0, the cause is not the label distribution.

not_available.reason: |S| = 1 on every slot (verify_k = 1), so 'idle is the max of S' has no comparison partner; the requested categories are structurally empty, not merely unobserved.  Reported as 0/8,774 with the degeneracy spelled out instead of a fabricated spread.

not_available.item: does the verified set cover all tied maxima / is the lowest-index rule load-bearing
not_available.reason: 0/19,772 slots have a tie at the maximum of teacher_scores, so the conditioned denominators are 0; the ratios are not_available rather than 0.

not_available.item: a causal attribution of the 5-6 pp residual to optimisation
not_available.reason: the dataset holds labels and teacher scores, not training trajectories or rollout states; separating 'label prior' from 'closed-loop fixed point' needs the matched ablation above, not another statistic on these files.

not_available.item: why the closed loop is worse for A0v, from this data alone
not_available.reason: pass rates, survival and death frames are not in the dataset; the only closed-loop numbers quoted here are copied from T04's DEV_EVAL / ACTION_MIX and are not recomputed.

the verified candidate is separated from every unverified one by at least 5.0 units (unverified_discount), so any 'rank of idle among all 18 scores' statistic is a property of the discount, not of the teacher's preference; it is therefore not reported as a preference measurement.

cannot_claim: that A0v's idle rebound is fully explained by the target distribution (it explains 39-49% of the measured arm gap)
that the verified-argmax objective is harmful in general (one 5,000-step run, seed 0, and the residual mechanism is unattributed)
that tie-breaking matters here (no tie at the maximum exists; |S| = 1 everywhere)
that idle share is a capability metric (T04's plan says it is a diagnostic)
that the executed column is a clean behaviour target (on 9,886 of 19,772 slots it is the second element of a two-frame-old plan)
that A0's lower idle is better play (both arms are 0/20 and the +4.5% survival is 20 dev episodes, one seed)
that the slot-1 disagreement is teacher non-determinism (the two columns are queried at different decision instants; no repeat-query control exists in this dataset)
that the dev evaluation distribution equals the training distribution (the frozen baseline B0 idles 45.81%/46.10% on dev against a 36.23% executed training prior)
